title: The Man Who Received Tomorrow's Newspaper
logline: A man starts receiving tomorrow's newspaper, and every edition erases a little more of him.

source.notes: Original story written for The Midnight Archive. No third-party text used.

narration.text: He lived alone. He had no subscription.
A misprint — until page nine reported his death.
Apartment fire. Friday. Three a.m. His name.
He booked a hotel across town.
Saturday's paper was at the front desk.
The fire happened anyway. Same building. Same hour. Different man.
The dead man was his neighbour, who'd knocked to warn him.
Elias spread every paper he'd saved across the floor.
All dated tomorrow. Each mentioned him less than the last.
First his job. Then his friends. Then the crossword.
By Friday, his photograph was a grey rectangle.
Saturday's paper arrived blank. Only the masthead remained.
The Midnight Archive: all the news that never was.
Elias finally understood. It wasn't predicting his future.
It was deciding what to keep.

final_line: It was deciding what to keep.
visual_style: Desaturated teal shadows, sodium-amber practical light, fine 16mm grain, 35mm lens, locked-off or slow dolly, one hard source per scene.
content_notes: Speculative fiction. The newspaper is a fictional device, not a factual claim about prediction or archives.
